runs.command: Create tiny top/child project under build/T-20260830-005/cand/* and run quartus_syn per candidate assignment; inspect QSF read errors.
runs.summary: Valid instance assignment is 'set_instance_assignment -name PARTITION <name> -to <path>' without -section_id. PARTITION_NAME and PARTITION_NETLIST_TYPE are invalid/unsupported in 21.4 QSF.
Tiny partition project with child partition successfully synthesized; Quartus reported 2 partitions after elaboration and synthesized root_partition + child sequentially.
Direct single-partition synthesis from a freshly fully-synthesized project fails because link_rtl_design -snapshot synthesis cannot find the required pre-synthesis snapshot.

Import QDB command accepted; no errors.

runs.command: quartus_sh --flow compile varImport -c varImport -start synthesis -end synthesis
runs.summary: After QDB import, synthesis still re-synthesized child partition from black-box RTL (stuck-at-GND), so the tested simple flow does not prove imported QDB replaces top-level RTL synthesis.

partition_plan.tier1: Single-project design partition assignments; creates partitions and lets quartus_syn synthesize each partition sequentially. Low effort, but whole-design analysis/elaboration still occurs first.
partition_plan.tier2: Standalone partition synthesis + quartus_cdb --export_partition/--import_partition bottom-up assembly. Required if 70GB OOM is in whole-design elaboration.
partition_plan.not_verified: Whether imported QDB partitions can be excluded from top-level synthesis; likely needs deeper block-based flow / preservation setting or fitter-stage import.

expected_benefits: Tier 2 bottom-up can reduce peak synthesis memory from one 70GB process to the largest standalone partition plus top-level glue.
Existing measurements suggest L1D ~3.6GB and AXI adapter ~0.9GB standalone, so most cache/core partitions may fit well below 70GB if individually synthesizable.
L2 remains the largest threat; it did not finish in >37min standalone before FPGA-B/C changes. Need rerun after reduced L2 geometry / potential multi-cycle/structural split.
A64_FP_SIMD=0 from FPGA-D provides a practical first-stage reduction; in Verilator it removed about 88-93% of elaboration size.
QDB export/import commands are available and may support incremental updates after only one partition changes.
risks: Simple single-project partition may not help if OOM occurs during elaboration (T-101 soc_only log stopped at Elaborating before partition synthesis messages).
Bottom-up flow is not fully validated: our tiny import still re-synthesized the black-box partition.
Cross-partition boundary complexity may increase fitting/timing effort and can harm Fmax if interfaces are not constrained.
Remote RTL is not synchronized with local main; any B5 partition experiment must first update the remote experimental copy.
L2 and soc_coh standalone synthesis have previously timed out; additional structural RTL splitting may be needed before partition assembly.
No fit/STA/SOF evidence is produced by this task; full FPGA-F acceptance still requires full flow after partitions are stable.
